items.text: I notice what is incorrect before I notice what is merely unfinished.
I feel responsible for improving systems that fall below a clear standard.
When I bend a rule, part of me keeps arguing the case afterward.
I quickly sense what support would make another person feel cared for.
Being needed can feel more comfortable than stating what I need.
I invest energy in relationships by becoming useful.
I naturally translate vague goals into visible wins.
I adjust my presentation to match what success looks like in the room.
Slowing down can make me wonder whether I am losing momentum or value.
I protect what feels distinctive about my inner life.
I can become absorbed in what is missing from an otherwise good experience.
Authenticity matters enough that I resist roles that feel generic.
I conserve time, energy, or privacy until I understand what a situation will demand.
Mastery makes me feel safer than improvising in public.
I often step back to observe before I enter the action.
My mind automatically tests plans for weak points and hidden consequences.
Trust grows for me when people prove consistent under pressure.
I can argue against my own preferred plan to make sure it will hold.
I keep multiple possibilities alive because closure can feel limiting.
When discomfort rises, my attention moves toward a more interesting option.
I generate energy by imagining what could happen next.
I would rather meet resistance directly than maneuver around it.
I protect my autonomy by making my position unmistakable.
I instinctively shield people I consider mine.
I can understand several sides so well that my own priority becomes blurry.
I delay conflict when keeping the atmosphere steady seems more important.
Once I settle into a comfortable rhythm, changing course takes extra force.

note: Original Citadel wording. Never present as a reproduction or substitute for any branded inventory.
